paper.title: A Multi-Arm Bandit Approach To Subset Selection Under Constraints

settings.name_in_paper: Subset selection with unknown qualities (CMAB with semi-bandit feedback and quality constraint)
unmapped: Super-arm reward is sum_{i in S}(R q_i - c_i) with known costs c_i and known constant R
Quality constraint: average unknown quality of selected subset must be >= alpha (constraint depends on unknown means)
the learner knows costs c_i, R and threshold alpha
Regret charges constant L in rounds where the constraint is violated
settings.definition_quote: We now consider a setting when $q_i$ are \emph{unknown} beforehand and can only be learned by selecting the agents. We model it as a CMAB problem with semi-bandit feedback and QC.

symbols.epsilon_1: tolerance on the average quality constraint

tuning: DPSS invoked with threshold alpha + epsilon_2 on UCB estimates

source.label: thm:tau
source.quote: For $\tau=\frac{3 \ln T}{2\epsilon_2^2}$, if each agent is explored $\tau$ number of rounds, then if we invoke \dpss\ with target threshold $\alpha+\epsilon_2$ and $\{(\hat{q}_i^t)^+\}_{i \in N}$ as the input, the QC is approximately met with high probability. \mathcal{P}(q_{av}^t<\alpha-\epsilon_1 | ... , t>\tau) \leq exp(-\epsilon_1^2t).

results.notes: Probability that the selected super-arm violates the approximate quality constraint at round t > tau. Not a regret bound; DPSS is O(2^n) time.

conditions: qualities satisfy epsilon_1-separatedness: no subset has average quality in (alpha - epsilon_1, alpha)
bound is on Reg_u(T), regret after tau rounds in rounds where QC is satisfied

source.label: thm:reg
source.quote: If qualities of the agents satisfy $\epsilon_1$-seperatedness, then $Reg_u(T)$ is bounded by $O(\ln T)$.

results.notes: Proof gives Reg_u(T) <= (6 ln T/(Delta_min/R)^2 + pi^2/3) n Delta_max, with n agents and super-arm gaps, adapted from CUCB analysis (Chen et al. 2013). Overall DPSS-UCB regret claimed O(ln T) by adding L*3ln T/(2 eps_2^2) exploration and O(1/T^a) violation term. Regret is the paper's constraint-aware regret, not standard pseudo-regret.
